definition: Generated content that is fluent and plausible but factually wrong or unsupported by the source material.
details: Hallucination arises when a model confidently produces text not grounded in retrieved evidence or its training data. It is one of the most consequential failure modes of LLMs, especially in medicine, law and journalism. A broad survey of the area organizes the causes and effects and surveys detection and mitigation strategies such as retrieval grounding and verification.
story: Picture a scoreboard at a science fair: you need a fair, agreed way to tell who actually won. In plain words: Generated content that is fluent and plausible but factually wrong or unsupported by the source material. Here is how it actually plays out: Hallucination arises when a model confidently produces text not grounded in retrieved evidence or its training data. A good metric is a ruler that does not bend when you lean on it. That shared ruler is Hallucination.

citation.title: Survey of Hallucination in Natural Language Generation
